records.claim: Leading and trailing identical bit counts wrap modulo 64 into 6 bits rather than saturating at 63 when val has 64 identical bits.
records.open_question: The paper does not state how 64 identical bits are handled in the 6-bit count fields: whether the count saturates at 63, wraps modulo 64, or counts bits following the first bit.

records.claim: Floating-point register format is supplied via an input parameter rather than dynamically inspecting register value MSBs.
records.open_question: The paper states that floating-point formats are classified by inspecting the most significant bits, but does not specify the exact bit inspection logic or encoding used to distinguish FP16, FP32, and FP64.

records.claim: For floating-point registers, extracted sign and exponent bits are placed into digest bits starting at bit 3 (FP16 at [5:3], FP32 at [8:3], FP64 at [11:3]) with bits [2:0] zeroed.
records.quote: extract the sign bit along with the most significant bits of the exponent.
records.why: Figure 6(b) and Section 4.2 show FP slices aligned at bit 3 leaving bits [2:0] unused.

records.claim: Condition-code flag digests replicate the four flag bits three times across all 12 bits.
records.quote: (3) For condition-code flags, we replicate the four flag bits three times to fill the 12-bit digest.
records.why: Section 4.2 specifies replicating the four flag bits three times to fill the 12-bit digest.

records.claim: The digest width is 12 bits.
records.quote: RUNLTS generates a 12-bit digest from each 64-bit register value, with the format depending on the register type.
records.why: Section 4.2 defines the digest width as 12 bits.

records.claim: The digest_width_bits parameter has a legal tuning range of [8, 16].
records.open_question: The paper sets the digest width to 12 bits and does not define or explore an alternative tuning range such as [8, 16].

records.claim: Stale digests are invalidated after 256 decoded instructions using an 8-bit decay counter.
records.quote: Consequently, RUNLTS invalidates each digest after 256 subsequent instructions have been decoded, ensuring that only up-to-date information influences future predictions.
records.why: Section 4.2 and Table 3 specify 256 instructions and an 8-bit decay counter per logical register.

records.claim: The decay_instruction_limit parameter has a legal tuning range of [64, 1024] pow2.
records.open_question: The paper establishes 256 instructions for decay invalidation but does not specify an alternative tuning range such as [64, 1024] pow2.

records.claim: Unit test 0 tests integer digest generation against the specified 12-bit XOR fold of trailing count, leading count, and 6 LSBs.
records.quote: (1) For integer registers, the digest encodes the count of leading zeros (or ones), the count of trailing zeros (or ones), and the six least significant bits, effectively capturing characteristics of addresses and round numbers.
records.why: The test inputs and expected digest match the 12-bit XOR fold defined in Section 4.2 and Figure 6(a).

records.claim: Unit test 1 tests replication of 4 flag bits three times to form a 12-bit digest.
records.quote: (3) For condition-code flags, we replicate the four flag bits three times to fill the 12-bit digest.
records.why: The test checks 4-bit flag replication (0x9 -> 0x999) matching Section 4.2 and Figure 6(c).

records.claim: Unit test 2 tests extraction and alignment of FP64 sign and exponent bits into digest bits [11:3].
records.quote: extract the sign bit along with the most significant bits of the exponent.
records.why: The test checks extraction of Value[63:55] shifted to bits [11:3] matching Figure 6(b).

records.claim: Unit test 3 tests digest invalidation via an 8-bit counter decrementing across 256 instructions.
records.quote: Consequently, RUNLTS invalidates each digest after 256 subsequent instructions have been decoded, ensuring that only up-to-date information influences future predictions.
records.why: The test checks the 256-instruction decay invalidation described in Section 4.2.

records.claim: Unit test 4 tests bank usefulness zero-suppression scaling where a bank with non-positive usefulness selects multiplier x0.
records.quote: That Sigma feeds a multiplier stage labelled "x0 or x2.5".
records.why: Figure 5(c) indicates that per-bank WT sums are gated by x0 or x2.5 based on usefulness, suppressing banks with non-positive usefulness.

records.claim: Unit test 6 tests random selection of one available register per bank during training to enable single-write-port RAMs.
records.quote: If several registers were available within the same bank, it randomly selects one of them for the update. Owing to this training method, each table in the register component also needs just a single write port.
records.why: Section 4.2 explicitly requires randomly selecting one available register in a bank during update to allow single-port RAMs.
